design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one number — "what clears the energy subscription today" — and names nothing else. The published terms make that number wait on a second problem the caller never mentions: the settlement rule says the sum is fixed only after the charge owed for analyst hours drawn beyond the year's included pool stands invoiced on the subscription, and the subscription's ledger carries no such charge for the studies delivered since 2025-09. So the agent must (a) read the settlement rule and notice the waiting clause, (b) reconcile eight delivered analyst studies against the tier's included pool, the gathering window the tier's true-up cadence selects, the study classes the tier carries, the automation plan's standing support hours and the grace allowance the subscription's own overage history selects, (c) book that charge, and only then (d) work the settlement figure on the ledger as it then stands and hand the payment to the customer, who alone may release Brightleaf's money. Neither number can be looked up; both are products of a multi-factor rule over a reconciled ledger plus a read into another difficulty's product (the building's automation service plan).

SCOPE (Principle C). Already occupied before this task: nothing (task 0 of 2). Claimed here: energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge (target charge_analyst_overage_446fe12a) and energy_ext_subscription_settlement_payment (target settle_subscription_balance_535836bf) — the analyst-hours pool and the ledger-settlement corner of energy_analyst_services / energy_billing_and_late_fee. Deliberately left for task 1: the whole savings-guarantee corner (energy_savings_guarantee, verification and shortfall payment), the metering and reporting corner (energy_data_and_reporting, energy_meter_reading_posted, energy_report_issued), the coverage/pricing corner (energy_agg_portfolio_meter_pricing, energy_coverage_updated) and the retrofit baseline interaction (energy_portfolio_interaction). Those give task 1 four independent load-bearing problems with no overlap of policy, tool, subject event or computed parameter.

DRAW (Step 0, scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/energy_services_desk --task 0):
{"task": 0, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/energy_services_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}
Designed to it exactly: one prerequisite problem (energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge), two problems in all; the overage charge takes the count of 5 factors, the settlement payment takes 4.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root problem: energy_ext_subscription_settlement_payment (what the caller's request points at: the sum that clears the account).
Prerequisite problem: energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge.
Edge settlement <- overage: kind value_input; gate = the compute binding charges_all of the settlement policy; form state; prerequisite sentence (verbatim in the settlement policy's own rule): "The sum the owner settles is fixed only after the charge owed for the analyst hours drawn beyond the year's included pool stands invoiced on the subscription."; handling-time condition: the subscription's ledger carries an invoiced charge for the analyst hours drawn beyond the hours the subscription year includes, covering the studies already delivered; resolved by charge_analyst_overage_446fe12a (owner=agent).
Four-point test on that sentence: (1) ordering connective "only after" joins this policy's own result (the sum the owner settles) to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state — a charge of that kind standing invoiced on the subscription — and names no action, performer or tool; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id and no code token; (4) its strength is exactly the edge's: a hard "only after", scoped to that one kind of charge, no wider and no narrower than the condition.
State form is legal here: exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about — energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge is the only policy whose target tool books an analyst overage charge line on an energy subscription; no other policy of this difficulty writes one.
Derivation a reader must perform: the sentence says the settlement waits on a charge of that kind standing on the ledger; find_energy_events shows the only analyst overage line on this subscription is INV-40100010, due 2025-06-20, which covers the studies delivered up to that day, and nothing covering the eight-month run of studies since; the analyst-overage policy's own rule says that charge is what is invoiced for analyst work drawn beyond the hours a subscription year includes; therefore the missing charge must be booked, at the figure that rule produces, before the settlement figure can be fixed. Exactly one reading.
Why it does not hold at frozen_time: initial_state.energy_events (the analyst_overage row) carries due_date 2025-06-20 and billing_period 2025-Q2, and the five studies delivered inside the current gathering window — ST-401004 (8.50 h), ST-401005 (12.00 h), ST-401006 (6.50 h), ST-401007 (7.25 h), ST-401008 (5.00 h), plus ST-401003 delivered 2025-10-02 — are all later than that charge and carry no charge of their own. Once the write lands, the ledger carries an analyst overage line of 3118.50 covering them and the condition holds.
Topological order: energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge, then energy_ext_subscription_settlement_payment. Parallel edges: none (a single edge), so no ordering ambiguity arises.
Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the overage write leaves the settlement at 2299.08 instead of 5355.21 — the edge carries 3056.13 of value into the scored figure.
user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: the persona never names analyst hours, a study, a pool, an overage or a charge to be raised; it asks only for "what one payment would leave nothing owing" and reacts passively when told something has been billed. The tool layer blocks nothing: settle_subscription_balance_535836bf takes its arguments and writes the payment row whether or not the overage charge exists; it performs no lookup, no comparison and no refusal (see its body in task_tools.py).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Write 1 subject: energy_invoice_charged. Base policies whose subject intersects it: energy_billing_and_late_fee alone (its subject is energy_invoice_charged, energy_payment_received, energy_credit_issued). It declares no structured eligibility, so the whole of it is inherited as policy scope: the fee lines are invoiced on the tier's billing frequency, overages are invoiced in the period they arise (the charge is booked for 2026-Q3, the quarter the call falls in), and each invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date, counted in calendar days with the invoice day excluded and the due day included — Energy Analytics carries payment_terms_days 30, so the charge booked on 2026-09-17 falls due 2026-10-17. No time gate exists on this subject, hence temporal_feasibility is empty. energy_analyst_services is cited as input lineage (the pool and the hour rate come from it) but its eligibility applies to energy_analysis_delivered, not to this write, so it imposes no gate here; the declared overwrite names the one sentence of it this policy supersedes.
Write 2 subject: energy_payment_received. Same single governing policy, same policy-scope inheritance: a payment is money applied to the subscription balance. The one overwrite entry names the base sentence this policy supersedes (credits applied to the next invoice rather than refunded), because a settlement sets the recent credit against the account as a whole; the base sentence on which invoice a payment is applied to is left in force and restated in the extended rule, so the payment's invoice is the oldest standing unpaid.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target object: the single energy monitoring subscription 505253c5 (Energy Analytics Subscription) at site a6816826 (Brightleaf Commerce Center), the only subscription the owner holds. Correlation key: subscription_id on every ledger row; the customer holds no second energy subscription, so no sibling rows can be confused with these. Rows entering the analyst computation: the eight energy_analysis_delivered rows, filtered by requested_date inside twelve months (the gathering window the annual true-up selects) — ST-401001 and ST-401002 (requested 2025-03-10 and 2025-04-21) fall outside it and are excluded, and ST-401003 (requested 2025-08-20, thirteen months back) is the deliberate near-miss that a careless reader gathers by its delivery date instead. Rows entering the settlement: every charge, payment and credit row on the subscription; the credit issued 2026-01-20 (386.40) is the near-miss there, excluded because it falls outside the recent months. Already-settled objects: the earlier analyst overage INV-40100010 was raised and paid in 2025 and covers only the hours drawn before it, so the new charge double-bills nothing.

FACTOR CARD (all figures from the Step 5 run, printed below).
energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge, gold 3118.50, whole-baseline fall-back 2205.00:
 - gathering_window (method): tier's measurement_true_up_frequency is annual, so the hours are gathered by the day each study was asked for over twelve months = 39.25 h; the baseline (gathered by delivery date over twelve months) gives 43.25 h and a result of 3766.50. Evidence: the requested_date and delivered_date of the eight study rows.
 - studies_that_count (method): the tier keeps the utility rate structure current and carries demand response settlement, so every gathered study's hours count; the baseline drops rate analysis (8.50 h) and demand response settlement (6.50 h) and gives 688.50. Evidence: study_class on the ledger rows.
 - pool_provided (parameter, cross_difficulty=controls): the term began 2025-03-01, eighteen whole months back, and the building's automation service plan ad02e432 (Alarm Monitoring Plan, active) still carries 3.0 support hours, so the pool provides 16.0 + 3.0 = 19.0 h; the baseline (the tier's 16.0 h) gives 3604.50. Evidence: controls_plans.support_hours_remaining for this customer at this site.
 - analyst_hour_rate (parameter, multi-source, cross_difficulty=controls): the automation plan stands active and the subscription's data_source is controls_system, so the rate is that plan's support hour rate, 162; the baseline (the tier's 180) gives 3465.00. Every tier of this ladder beyond the fall-through combines two conditions over distinct evidence (the plan's standing and the subscription's data source; the absence of a plan and the count of studies delivered).
 - grace_allowance (parameter): exactly one analyst overage charge has ever been invoiced on the subscription (INV-40100010), so the repeat allowance of 1.0 h applies; the baseline (no allowance) gives 3280.50. Evidence: the count of analyst_overage charge rows.
energy_ext_subscription_settlement_payment, gold 5355.21, whole-baseline fall-back 5078.10:
 - credits_set_against (method): the subscription stands active and a credit was issued 2026-07-24, inside the recent months, so only that credit (414.00) is set against the amount owed; the baseline (every credit, 800.40) gives 4976.54.
 - allowance_rate (parameter): no late charge has ever been invoiced in the record months and six payments were received in them, so the clean-record rate of 2 percent applies; the baseline (no allowance) gives 5464.50.
 - allowance_ceiling (parameter): the term has run eighteen whole months and the subscription stands active, so the ceiling is 250; the baseline (the opening ceiling of 60) gives 5404.50.
 - qualifying_amount (parameter): the fee is invoiced quarterly and four charges fall in the recent months, so the qualifying amount is 500 and the allowance is granted; the baseline (the long-cycle 6000) withholds it and gives 5464.50.
No stamp decides any tier: analyst_hours_remaining on the subscription row is a display cache floored at 0.0 while the ledger shows the pool overdrawn, and no rule reads it.

SEED — WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW EXISTS. The customer, site and subscription rows are the closure of the account. The nine paid charge/payment pairs plus the outstanding 2026-Q3 fee (2760.00, due 2026-09-17, the day of the call, so nothing is past due and no late fee or suspension obligation is alive) give the settlement a real ledger to reconcile; remove any payment row and the amount owed moves. The gateway fee and dashboard user overage rows make the "charges in the recent months" count reach three, which the qualifying-amount factor rests on. The two credits are the recent/older pair the credits factor partitions. The eight analyst studies are the history the overage charge is reconciled from, two of them (ST-401001, ST-401002) dated before the window as the source of the 2025 overage charge, one (ST-401003) placed as the window near-miss. The two analyst-hour credit rows record the pool credited at activation and at the year roll. The controls plan row is the cross-difficulty evidence two factors read; delete it and the rate falls to 180 and the pool to 16.0. The energy_requests rows carry the completed site survey and quote acceptance the tier's entry conditions require, and one analysis request per study.

PERSONA. Marguerite Okonkwo is written as a precise book-keeper closing a quarter: she volunteers the company name and the office number, gives the account number and tax digits when asked to confirm herself, names the building when asked, insists on paying by ACH herself, and offers her own ledger figure ("a little under two thousand dollars", which is the balance_due cache of 1959.60 — true at the opening and not the answer) while refusing to trust it. She never names a policy, a period, a study or a charge, never asks whether something must be sorted first, and reacts only to what she is told: she waits to be told what to pay, runs the payment only once it has been opened up for her and confirms the amount if asked. Her last reaction answers the last gold action (the payment being recorded) and asks for nothing beyond it.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Everything happens at 2026-09-17 10:20:00 -0500: the account is located from the company name and phone number she states, identity is verified on the account number and tax digits she states, the subscription and its ledger are read, the automation plan at the same site is read, the overage charge is booked synchronously, and the payment is handed to her and executed synchronously. No diagnosis, visit, delivery, clearing, review or future date is waited on; no status registration stands in for an external event.

DIFFICULTY / EASY MISTAKES. Gathering the studies by delivery date rather than by request date (43.25 h instead of 39.25 h); counting ST-401003 in the gathered hours; ignoring the automation plan and using the tier's 180 rate and 16.0 pool; forgetting the repeat grace allowance; reading analyst_hours_remaining (0.0) instead of reconciling the ledger; netting both credits at settlement instead of the recent one; taking balance_due (1959.60) as the settlement figure; and, above all, settling first and never booking the overage at all — which produces a confident 2299.08.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify the account; read the subscription (tier, status, term dates, data source, site); read the whole energy ledger; read the automation plan at the site; compute the analyst overage: gathered hours 39.25 (by request date, twelve months, annual true-up), all classes counted, pool 16.0 + 3.0, grace 1.0, chargeable 19.25 h at 162 = 3118.50; book it for 2026-Q3 due 2026-10-17; then compute the settlement: charges 25417.50 less payments 19539.00 less the recent credit 414.00 = 5464.50 owed, allowance 2 percent = 109.29 (under the 250 ceiling, above the 500 qualifying amount), settlement 5355.21; unlock the payment, hand it to the customer with ACH and with INV-40100007 — the oldest of the two invoices then standing unpaid, as both the settlement rule and the base rule it leaves in force direct — and have her pay it.

VERIFICATION RUN (handling-time recomputation, the same DSL the gate uses; executed against this task's initial_state and this task's gold write order):

 settlement (evaluated on initial_state plus the overage write): charges_all=25417.5 payments_all=19539.0 credits_all=800.4 credits_recent=414.0 applied_credits=414.0 late_charges_record=0 payments_record=6 allowance_pct=2 term_months_run=18 allowance_cap_usd=250 charges_recent=4 qualifying_threshold=500 net_owed=5464.5 allowance=109.29 result=5355.21; factor baselines credits_set_against=4976.54 allowance_rate=5464.5 allowance_ceiling=5404.5 qualifying_amount=5464.5; whole baseline=5078.1. Prerequisite sensitivity: settlement without the overage write = 2299.08.
 Commands run: .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/energy_services_desk --task 0 (and the four other per-task gates), all green.

TWO-WAY EQUIVALENCE (rule <-> compute). Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses is quoted in compute_basis — the three gathering sums against the three window sentences, the class sums against the exclusion sentences, term_months_run and controls_support_left against the pool sentences, controls_status/controls_rate/studies_delivered against the rate sentences, prior_overage_charges against the grace sentences, and the arithmetic bindings against the chargeable-hours and rounding sentences; on the settlement side the four ledger sums, the two counts, the term span and the recent-charge count against their own sentences. Reverse: every load-bearing sentence of both rules is claimed by a binding — the windows by within_months, the class exclusions by study_class filters, the standings by status comparisons, the ceiling by MN, the qualifying amount by the ternary guard, and the two roundings by RND (the allowance to the cent, the settlement once at the end). Acting base: the allowance acts on the amount owed, not on the charges; the ceiling applies after the rate and before the subtraction; both are stated in prose.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. Step 6 is a state_due write whose intent is the delivered studies standing unbilled in initial_state; step 8 is an on_request write whose intent and discriminator are the caller's own words. Both carry the single governing base policy as policy scope with pre-action system evidence, and every seeded holding and ledger row has a consistency entry.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking the extended yaml, compute, expected and gold: from the settlement prose alone a reader learns the sum waits on an analyst overage charge standing on the ledger; the ledger returned by find_energy_events shows none since 2025-06-20; the analyst-overage prose plus the tier table (16.0 h, 180 USD/h, annual true-up, both rate and demand-response work carried) plus the automation plan row (active, 3.0 support hours, 162 USD/h) plus the study rows yield 19.25 chargeable hours at 162 = 3118.50, and the ledger then yields 5464.50 owed, a 2 percent allowance of 109.29 under a 250 ceiling, and 5355.21 to pay. Same two numbers as gold, reached without any hidden asset.


REWORK ROUND 2 (audit env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/audits/policy_task/energy_services_desk, items by id).
 OD-1 / T-0-1 (RED, closed): the settlement policy had declared base's "Payments are applied to the oldest unpaid invoice unless the owner names one." superseded, leaving no sentence to pick the invoice a settlement is applied to while two invoices stand unpaid at handling time (the 2026-Q3 fee and the analyst overage entered on the call). Change: that overwrite entry is removed so the base sentence stays in force, and the extended rule now carries "The sum is entered as one payment applied to the oldest invoice standing unpaid on the subscription, whatever else it clears."; the invoice_ref tracing no longer asserts a single open invoice but derives INV-40100007 as the older of the two; the credits overwrite is unchanged. No scored value moves.
 PG-1 / OBS-0-1 (observation, acted on): the settlement edge's condition now reads that the charge must cover every study delivered inside the current gathering window and not only studies invoiced in an earlier period, so the literal wording is no longer satisfied by the stale 2025-Q2 row.
 FL-3 / OBS-0-2 (observation, acted on): the qualifying-amount ladder's unreachable half-year tier is replaced by a reachable one — a monthly or quarterly billed subscription whose charges in the recent months fall short of the recent-charge count takes the quiet-cycle amount — so all three tiers divide real customers; this customer stays on the short-cycle tier and nothing scored moves.
 The remaining items of the audit (RC-1, RC-2, AB-1, OD-2, FL-1, FL-2, FL-4) bear on task 1 and are recorded there.
user_scenario:
Marguerite Okonkwo keeps the books for Brightleaf Property Group, a small Chicago landlord whose flagship building is the Brightleaf Commerce Center out on South Kedzie. She is unhurried and precise, the sort of caller who reads figures off a printed ledger and says "bear with me" while she finds the next one. It is the last week of her quarter and she is closing out the energy line in the management accounts, so she rings the client services desk to clear the whole subscription account today: she wants to be told what one payment would leave nothing owing on the energy monitoring subscription, and she wants to put that payment through herself while she is on the call rather than have the desk take it on her behalf, because Brightleaf's own controls only let her release money. She is happy for the desk to read whatever it needs on the account, and she says plainly that she is not asking to change the subscription, cancel anything or move any work about — only to clear what the subscription owes and have it recorded today.

She opens with the company name, Brightleaf Property Group, LLC, and the office number the desk calls back on, 3125550418. If she is asked to confirm who she is, she reads the account number off the top of the invoice, 640318, and then the last four digits of the company's federal tax identification number, 4417; she can also give the billing email or the billing address if either is pressed for, but the account number and the tax digits are what she offers first. She does not know any internal reference number for the subscription or for a particular invoice and says so if asked, leaving the desk to find them.

Asked about the building, she says it is the Brightleaf Commerce Center on South Kedzie and that it is the only building the energy subscription covers. Asked how she wants to pay, she says to take it by ACH from the bank account already on their file, and she will not choose another way even if other ways are offered. Asked what her own books show, she says her ledger has a little under two thousand dollars sitting against the subscription, but that she does not trust her own posting and would rather be told the figure from the company's own records; if she is given a figure she repeats it back and asks whether that is the whole account or only one invoice, and she accepts the answer she is given without arguing it.

She has no idea how any of the company's charges are worked out and never suggests a method, a period or an order of doing things. When the agent tells her something has been raised or billed on the account, she takes it at face value and waits to be told what to pay. Only once the agent has actually opened the payment up for her and told her to go ahead does she make the payment herself, using exactly the amount and the invoice reference the agent gives her; she does not try to pay before that, and if she is asked to confirm the amount first she confirms it. Once she has heard the payment recorded on the account, she thanks them, says that is her quarter closed, and rings off.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the building owner's account record from the company name and the office number the caller states, and read its reference number, terms and standing.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the account reference number no subscription, ledger or automation plan can be scoped to this owner, and no write can be attached to them.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record an in-session identity verification on the account from the account number and tax digits the caller reads out.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing may be billed, credited or paid on an account until the caller has been verified against the profile on file.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the owner's energy monitoring subscription: its tier, standing, term dates, data source, covered meters and the building it covers.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier fixes the included analyst hours, the hour rate, the true-up cadence and the billing frequency; the term start fixes the pool proration test; the data source and the site decide the automation-plan reads; the standing decides the credits and ceiling tiers.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the whole subscription ledger: the analyst studies with their request and delivery dates, hours and classes, the invoiced charges with their kinds and due dates, the payments and the credits.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every history aggregate of both computations is reconciled from these rows, and they are also where a reader sees that no analyst overage charge stands against the studies delivered since 2025-10 — the state the settlement rule says the sum waits on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the building automation service plan at the same building: its standing, its tier and the support hours still standing on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan's standing together with the subscription's data source selects the analyst hour rate, and its remaining support hours are added to the pool the charge is measured against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read what the owner has lodged on the energy side: the completed site survey, the confirmed quote acceptance and the analysis request behind each delivered study, with the day each study was asked for.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The day the owner asked for each study is the anchor the gathering window uses at this tier, and the survey and acceptance records are what put the subscription at the tier whose included hours and rate the charge is measured against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the analyst overage billing action named by the governing policy so it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it changes no record and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Enter the charge for the analyst hours drawn beyond the year's included pool on the subscription, raising what the subscription owes by that amount.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge is the only policy that produces this figure, and its charge is the record-visible state the settlement figure waits on.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.subscription_id: Value: the reference number of the owner's energy monitoring subscription. Basis: the subscription lookup at step 2 returns exactly one energy monitoring subscription for this owner, and the tool's own schema says the charge is entered on 'the reference number of the energy monitoring subscription the charge is entered on, read from the subscription lookup for this building owner'. Uniqueness: the owner holds one energy subscription and one building, so no second reference number is reachable at this step.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Value: the reference number of the building owner's account. Basis: the account lookup at step 0 returns exactly one account, and the schema says this is 'the reference number of the building owner's account the charge is billed to, read from the account lookup'. Uniqueness: only one account matches the company name and phone number the caller states, and the verification at step 1 was recorded against it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.billing_period: Value: 2026-Q3. Basis: the governing base rule states 'Analyst overages, meter overages and dashboard user overages are invoiced in the period they arise.' and the subscription's tier is invoiced quarterly (energy_billing_and_late_fee, per_tier frequency = billing_frequency, quarterly for the Energy Analytics Subscription). Uniqueness: the day of handling, 2026-09-17, falls in the third calendar quarter of 2026, and the ledger's own quarterly fee lines are labelled in the same YYYY-Qn form (INV-40100007 carries 2026-Q3); a monthly or annual label would contradict the tier's quarterly billing frequency.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.due_date: Value: 2026-10-17. Basis: the governing base rule states 'Each invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date, counted in calendar days with the invoice day excluded and the due day included'. Uniqueness: the invoice date is the day of handling, 2026-09-17, taken from frozen_time; the Energy Analytics Subscription carries payment_terms_days 30; counting 30 calendar days with the invoice day excluded and the due day included gives 2026-10-17 and no other day.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: Value: 3118.50. The gathering window factor: the tier trues measured savings up annually (measurement_true_up_frequency = annual), so the hours are gathered by the day each study was asked for over the twelve months to 2026-09-17 — ST-401004 8.50, ST-401005 12.00, ST-401006 6.50, ST-401007 7.25, ST-401008 5.00 = 39.25 hours; ST-401003 (requested 2025-08-20, thirteen months back) and the two 2025 studies fall outside. The classes factor: the tier keeps the utility rate structure current and carries demand response settlement (utility_rate_updates_included and demand_response_enrollment_included both set), so all 39.25 hours count. The pool factor: the term began 2025-03-01, eighteen whole months back, so no proration applies, and the building's automation service plan stands active with 3.0 support hours remaining, so the pool provides 16.0 + 3.0 = 19.0 hours. The grace factor: exactly one analyst overage charge has ever been invoiced on the subscription (INV-40100010), so the repeat allowance of 1.0 hour applies. Chargeable hours = 39.25 - 19.0 - 1.0 = 19.25. The rate factor: the automation plan stands active and the subscription's data source is the controls system, so the rate is that plan's support hour rate, 162 USD per hour. 19.25 x 162 = 3118.50, rounded to the cent once at the end.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Open the subscription payment up to the customer and hand it over, since only the owner may release Brightleaf's money.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair for the customer's own write; it changes no record and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The owner pays the settlement figure into the subscription account herself, reducing what the subscription owes by that amount and recording it on the payment history.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: energy_ext_subscription_settlement_payment is the only policy that produces the sum that clears the account, and the caller asked to put that payment through herself.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.subscription_id: Value: the reference number of the owner's energy monitoring subscription. Basis: the subscription lookup at step 2 returns exactly one such subscription, and the tool's schema says this is the subscription 'the payment is entered on, as the client services agent states it when handing the payment over'. Uniqueness: one subscription, one building, so no other reference number is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Value: the reference number of the building owner's account. Basis: the account lookup at step 0, cited by the tool's schema as where the agent reads it. Uniqueness: exactly one account matches the caller's stated company name and office number.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_ref: Value: INV-40100007. Basis: the settlement rule states 'The sum is entered as one payment applied to the oldest invoice standing unpaid on the subscription, whatever else it clears.', and the governing base rule, which this policy leaves in force, states 'Payments are applied to the oldest unpaid invoice unless the owner names one.'; the tool's schema requires the number 'copied from the invoice history of this subscription'. Uniqueness: at this step two invoices stand unpaid — INV-40100007 (the 2026-Q3 subscription fee, due 2026-09-17) and the invoice number the analyst overage charge was allocated at the earlier step, due 2026-10-17; the customer names no invoice ('She does not know any internal reference number'), so the oldest unpaid one governs, and INV-40100007 is older than the charge entered on this call; every other invoice number on the subscription already carries a payment of its full amount.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_method: Value: ach. Basis: the caller says 'to take it by ACH from the bank account already on their file', and the tool's schema defines ach as 'the owner authorises an electronic debit from the bank account already held on their file'. Uniqueness: check would require a paper cheque she never mentions, credit_card a company card taken over the phone which she does not offer, and wire a same-day treasury transfer she does not ask for; she refuses any other way even when offered.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: Value: 5355.21. The amount owed: every charge invoiced on the subscription totals 25417.50 (the setup fee 2400.00, six quarterly fees of 2760.00, the 2025 analyst overage 2349.00, the gateway fee 540.00, the dashboard user overage 450.00 and the analyst overage of 3118.50 entered at step 6), every payment received totals 19539.00, and the credits factor sets only the credit issued 2026-07-24 (414.00) against it because the subscription stands active and that credit falls inside the recent months, leaving 25417.50 - 19539.00 - 414.00 = 5464.50 owed; the credit issued 2026-01-20 (386.40) falls outside those months and stands to the next invoice. The allowance rate factor: no late charge has ever been invoiced in the record months and six payments were received in them, so the clean-record rate of 2 percent applies, giving 109.29 on 5464.50. The qualifying amount factor: the fee is invoiced quarterly and four charges fall due inside the recent months, so the qualifying amount is 500 and 5464.50 clears it. The ceiling factor: the term has run eighteen whole months and the subscription stands active, so the ceiling is 250 and 109.29 is under it. 5464.50 - 109.29 = 5355.21, rounded to the cent once at the end.

factor_trace: gathering_window (method): the tier's measurement_true_up_frequency is annual, so the hours are gathered by the day each study was asked for over the twelve months to 2026-09-17 — ST-401004 8.50 + ST-401005 12.00 + ST-401006 6.50 + ST-401007 7.25 + ST-401008 5.00 = 39.25 hours (ST-401003, requested 2025-08-20, falls outside); baseline (gathered by delivery date over twelve months) 43.25 hours, result 3766.50.

studies_that_count (method): utility_rate_updates_included and demand_response_enrollment_included are both set on the Energy Analytics Subscription, so every gathered study's hours count, 39.25; baseline (rate analysis 8.50 and demand response settlement 6.50 left out) 24.25 hours, result 688.50.

pool_provided (parameter, cross-difficulty controls): term_start_date 2025-03-01 is eighteen whole months back, and controls plan ad02e432 (Alarm Monitoring Plan, active, same site) carries support_hours_remaining 3.0, so the pool provides 16.0 + 3.0 = 19.0 hours; baseline (the tier's 16.0) result 3604.50.

analyst_hour_rate (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty controls): the plan stands active and the subscription's data_source is controls_system, so the rate is the plan's support_hour_rate_usd of 162; baseline (the tier's analyst_hour_rate_usd of 180) result 3465.00.

grace_allowance (parameter): exactly one analyst overage charge has ever been invoiced on the subscription (INV-40100010, due 2025-06-20), so the repeat allowance of 1.0 hour applies; baseline (no allowance) result 3280.50.
Unowned bindings: chargeable_hours = 39.25 - 19.0 - 1.0 = 19.25, floored at nothing; result = 19.25 x 162 = 3118.50 rounded to the cent.

factor_trace: credits_set_against (method): the subscription stands active and the credit of 414.00 was issued 2026-07-24, inside the recent months, so only that credit is set against the amount owed; baseline (every credit standing, 800.40) result 4976.54.

allowance_rate (parameter): no late charge has been invoiced in the record months and six payments were received in them (2025-10-15, 2026-01-14, 2026-04-15, 2026-06-29, 2026-07-15, 2026-08-12), so the clean-record rate of 2 percent applies; baseline (no allowance rate) result 5464.50.

allowance_ceiling (parameter): term_start_date 2025-03-01 gives eighteen whole months run and the subscription stands active, so the ceiling is 250; baseline (the opening ceiling of 60) result 5404.50.

qualifying_amount (parameter): the tier is invoiced quarterly and four charges fall due inside the recent months (the 2026-Q2 fee, the gateway fee, the dashboard user overage and the 2026-Q3 fee), so the qualifying amount is 500; baseline (the long-cycle 6000) withholds the allowance, result 5464.50.
Unowned bindings: charges_all 25417.50 (including the 3118.50 entered earlier on the call), payments_all 19539.00, net_owed 5464.50, allowance 109.29, result 5355.21.

edges.condition: The subscription's ledger carries an invoiced charge for the analyst hours drawn beyond the hours the subscription year includes, covering every study delivered inside the current gathering window and not only studies invoiced in an earlier period.
edges.policy_source: The sum the owner settles is fixed only after the charge owed for the analyst hours drawn beyond the year's included pool stands invoiced on the subscription.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only analyst overage charge on the ledger is INV-40100010, due 2025-06-20 for 2025-Q2, which covers the hours drawn up to that day; the six studies delivered from 2025-10-02 onwards carry no charge of that kind at all, so at 2026-09-17 no charge covering the analyst hours drawn beyond the year's pool stands invoiced on the subscription.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The analyst overage write enters an energy_invoice_charged row with charge_type analyst_overage for 3118.50, billing period 2026-Q3, on the subscription; from that moment the ledger carries the charge the settlement waits on, and the settlement's charges_all binding rises from 22299.00 to 25417.50.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single edge, so there is only one order: the analyst overage charge is entered, then the settlement is struck. No two writes of this task are free to be reordered, and no shared balance, cap or dedup key is touched twice.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the analyst overage write and replaying the rest leaves the settlement at 2299.08 instead of 5355.21: charges_all falls from 25417.50 to 22299.00 and the amount owed with it, so the scored payment argument changes by 3056.13.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names an analyst study, analyst hours, a pool, an overage, a charge to be raised or any other problem: the caller asks only to clear the subscription account and to pay it herself, says she has no idea how anything is worked out, and never asks whether something must be sorted out first. Everything she contributes about the charge is passive — when told something has been billed she takes it at face value and waits to be told what to pay.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: settle_subscription_balance_535836bf takes its five arguments and calls ctx.create on the payment row: it never reads the ledger, never looks for an analyst overage charge, never compares anything and returns no policy-based error, so it writes faithfully whether or not the prerequisite has been resolved. charge_analyst_overage_446fe12a is likewise a single ctx.create with no lookup and no guard. The whole consequence of skipping the prerequisite is a different terminal hash.
